conviction_note: The company's own consensus (16 Oct, 17 analysts) is the bar and every line I can source is already in it: NII above the guide, a smaller buyback, CET1 at the floor of its range. What the release adds is the size of the buyback and the new NII guide, and nothing I found says which way those land against a bar that already expects a smaller buyback. So the findings sum to +0.1 and p_up is 52. abs_move_pct is 5.0, from the name's own results-day moves (median about 4%, Q3 prints -2.3/+3.1/+4.6) plus a likely guidance change. The UK Budget on 28 Oct sits outside the window.

findings.finding: The buyback is the line that can surprise, and the setup leans to a small one or none. Consensus CET1 is 14.1%, only 0.1pt above the floor of the 14-14.5% range. The FVOCI reserve had already fallen about $1.1bn in H1, BofA expects a tougher capital quarter from the value change in HSBC's hedging debt instruments, GS expects $0.5bn (down from $1bn), and long yields spiked further after quarter end (UK 30y above 6% in early October).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 4 Aug 2026: $1bn buyback, below hopes per SCMP/HK coverage; London -0.8%. 5 May 2026 (1Q26, $0.4bn fraud ECL, buybacks still paused): -5.86%. 28 Oct 2025 (3Q25): +4.6%. The buyback figure has repeatedly been the swing factor.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The GS $0.5bn and BofA capital calls are in wire copy, and the stock has fallen about 15% from its August peak, partly on this. What remains unpriced is the tail: if the market had fully priced a zero buyback, the 20-day drawdown would not be so evenly blamed on macro (yields, the UK budget) in the HK and UK coverage. Sized small and negative because CET1 has no room above the floor and the October yield spike lands after quarter end, which favours guarded 4Q capital commentary.
findings.independence: FVOCI reserve move in the company's own interim statement of changes in equity (-$319m to -$1,460m): https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/hsbc-holdings--hsba/hsbc-holdings-plc-2026-interim-results/9702338 ; GS $0.5bn call: https://www.thestandard.com.hk/finance/article/346430/HSBC-Q3-profit-forecast-to-rise-33-percent-net-interest-income-and-buyback-in-focus ; yields: https://finance.biggo.com/news/2a208372-34db-42f0-9289-dc0f3b18204d

findings.finding: The company's own consensus already has FY26 banking NII at $46.93bn against the 'at least $46bn' guide and 3Q at $11.9bn. After the September Fed hike and a steeper curve, a guide raise is likely, but a raise only to about $47bn is already in the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The NII guide was raised at the 4 Aug 2026 interims (to at least $46bn) and the stock fell 0.8% because the buyback dominated. On days with large moves (+7.94% on FY25, 25 Feb 2026) new targets were in play.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the consensus PDF is public and already sits above the guide. Only a raise above about $47bn (e.g. 'around $47.5bn') would be news. GS's own upgrade was +0.3%, which says the sell-side sees little upside beyond consensus. Kept small and positive because the rate backdrop (Fed hike, higher reinvestment yields on the structural hedge) favours an upward revision rather than a cut.
findings.independence: GS expects banking NII +3% q/q and raised its 2026-28 NII forecasts 0.3/1/1%: https://www.thestandard.com.hk/finance/article/346430/HSBC-Q3-profit-forecast-to-rise-33-percent-net-interest-income-and-buyback-in-focus

findings.finding: The $1bn buyback ended on 28 Sep, so HSBC had no repurchase bid in the market through the October drawdown (about -10%). Any new programme announced 27 Oct restarts a daily company bid into a de-rated, 13-week-low tape where retail commentary is already asking 'a bargain again at 1,360p?'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None separable; the stock fell 9.8% in the 20 sessions with no buyback running.
findings.why_not_priced: Inference only. The run-up is the free control and this finding partly restates it. If the de-rating had already reversed, the stock would not be sitting at 13-week lows on 22-23 Oct (1,352p close).

findings.finding: Restructuring noise likely in notable items: FT-reported cuts of nearly 70% of UK wealth financial advisers in an AI push (reported 7 Oct) point to further restructuring costs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Restructuring notables ($0.3bn in 1H26) have not moved the stock on their own.
findings.why_not_priced: Small and below the line; it already sits inside management's $2bn simplification-savings programme, so its only path to the guide is through costs that are already guided.
findings.independence: https://www.thestandard.com.hk/finance/article/346430/HSBC-Q3-profit-forecast-to-rise-33-percent-net-interest-income-and-buyback-in-focus (sidebar headline 07-10-2026: 'HSBC plans job cuts across UK wealth business in AI push, FT reports')

findings.finding: Asset-management reshuffle: The Standard (26 Oct) reports, citing sources, that Hang Seng Investment Management will merge into HSBC's asset-management business, and Bloomberg (20 Oct, via The Standard) that HSBC is seeking to replace AM CEO Nicolas Moreau. Both could be confirmed alongside the results as Hang Seng synergy delivery.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior reaction on this line; the Hang Seng synergies were guided at $0.5bn plus a $0.4bn stretch on the 2Q call.
findings.why_not_priced: Immaterial to group earnings. It is a sourced report rather than a company statement, and it is filed only because it may appear in the release.

findings.finding: HSBC no longer controls INKA (Internationale Kapitalanlagegesellschaft mbH) as of 8 Oct 2026, per its own TR-1 filing, so the German disposal has completed. Any gain or loss from it is a 4Q notable item that the 3Q release may only flag.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Disposal notables (Malta -$0.3bn, UK life -$0.2bn in 1H26) did not move the stock on their own.
findings.why_not_priced: Immaterial and below operating income, with no path to the guide; sized at zero.

outside_window.finding: The UK Autumn Budget on 28 Oct may raise the bank surcharge (rumoured 3% to 8%). About 20% of HSBC's group profit is surcharge-eligible; UBS puts a doubling at a 3-4% profit hit for the domestic banks, so the hit to HSBC is smaller. It resolves the day after the window, and management commentary on 27 Oct will not settle it.
Standard Chartered reports 3Q on 28 Oct (BofA expects a cleaner print with possible guidance upgrade) - peer read-across lands after the window.

baseline_tension: The findings are roughly neutral and do not cut against the lean. The run-up of -9.8% (20d) and -13.2% (60d) says the capital and Budget fears are largely priced. The capital finding agrees with what drove that fall, so it adds little, and the two small positives (guide raise, buyback bid restarting) mostly restate the de-rating.
language_note: Domestic UK retail/adviser sources (interactive investor, 15 Oct; The Twelfth Magpie, 25 Oct) carried BofA's specific call that 3Q would be 'tougher' because the value change in HSBC's interest-rate-hedging debt instruments hits the capital available for buybacks, plus the surcharge-eligible profit share (20% for HSBC) and the UBS sizing of a surcharge doubling. The English HK/wire previews (The Standard, BigGo) gave the GS $0.5bn figure. Each half carried a different broker's version of the same capital thesis, which is corroboration rather than new information

Investegate's RNS mirror carried two things no preview mentioned: the TR-1 showing INKA left HSBC control on 8 Oct, and the exact buyback conclusion date of 28 Sep, which leaves no company bid through October
lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide' and 'you were too small about the move': raised abs_move_pct from 4.5 to 5.0, since an NII guide change is likely and the buyback is new, and the name's own results-day moves run at a median of about 4% with a -8.4% to +7.9% tail; the findings were left unchanged
'A zero on a register that read is the truncation floor': restated positioning_check to say there is no anchor and that priced_lean is the run-up; no finding moved
'Cash can outweigh a raised guide' (the bank analogue is capital and the buyback against NII): confirmed the buyback finding as the swing line over the NII guide finding; sizes unchanged
